newsitem.title: USA: White House criticizes Republican stance on taxes.
newsitem.headline: White House criticizes Republican stance on taxes.

text.p: The common stance on taxes worked out by House and Senate Republicans moves in the wrong direction, White House spokesman Mike McCurry said Thursday.

"We respectfully heard the outline of their proposed bill, but our initial assessment is that in most important respects it moves in the wrong direction, not the right direction," McCurry told reporters.

Asked if the White House was discouraged about the chances of enacting balanced-budget legislation before Congress goes on vacation in August, McCurry replied: "Not discouraged -- it just means that we are looking ahead at some hard work and hard negotiating before we get a final version of a tax bill that will be enacted into law."
McCurry said that White House officials were expected to hold talks with congressional negotiators on Thursday.

Congressional Republicans, Democrats and the White House are trying to work out compromise legislation to enact the balanced-budget agreement that Clinton worked out with the Republican leaders of Congress in May.
